Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8286022
Permit API: 063-35508
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Young Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/20/2026
Comments: On 8/19/2026 Jason Branan (OGI) notified Caleb Peterson and I about a potential brine release in a farm field off Lebanon Road, Saltsburg, Pa. We went to the site at 9:20 am. There was a black, plastic riser in a field, and there appeared to be brine spilling out onto the ground. We used the soil conductivity probe and tested the release area. The soil conductivity was 6.62 ms/cm. There were no gas wells in view near the riser, but we did observe a pipeline marker for UGI Energy Services nearby. We notified UGI about the spill. We also notified Diversified about the spill because they operate wells nearby. At 2:53 pm, Diversified called and said the release was from a brine transfer line for coalbed methane wells in the area. Caleb and I returned to the release location on 8/20/2026. The riser was no longer filled with brine. The spill area was approximately 60 feet long, and the spill amount is greater than 42-gallons. The closest Diversified coalbed methane well near the spill location is 063-35508.Due to the spill being greater than 42-gallons, the Department is requesting remediation and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Violations are noted below.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/23/2025 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Middlebury Township, Tioga county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/23/2025
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8259975
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/23/2025
Comments: On 12/23/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 33 degrees, overcast and lightly snowing when I arrived on location. Snowfall had impacted the region in the last 24 hours, depositing approximately 3 inches on the location. The original south pad for the Taft 851 1V well has been returned to original grade. The plugged well monument witnessed during previous inspections was not visible. Stormwater diversion berms have been installed north and west of the original pad. Due to snow cover, stabilization could not be assessed for the constructed areas. Patterson drilling rig #805 has been towered down and removed from the north pad, having drilled eight new gas wells to total depth. Most of the drilling equipment has been removed from the site. Crews were on site, cleaning up the surface of the drilling mats and pumping out the well cellars. 40 frac tanks, seven rolloff dumpsters, two vac boxes, and four cement silos remain on site. Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Sand separators and two frac tanks remain attached to these wells. I did witness a 4' x 16' x 2" deep puddle of liquid on the unprotected pad surface north of the five GPUs that field tested at 1953 uS conductance. I reported this to a maintenance worker who relayed it to the Seneca site manager, Cory Miller.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water/ice. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1600 hours.

Comments: On February 2, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection at the Sinay well pad in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3490035 where violations appeared to have been abated and were therefore, closed. The only violation left outstanding was pursuant to the PPC plan that was deemed to be inadequate. As of the date of this inspection, the Department awaits the newly revised PPC plan that was said to be in the works in the NOV response to IR 3442875.The following was observed:The act 9 sign was clearly visible and unobstructed by view from vegetation (see photo 1). The CFS that was added around the storm drain in response to IR 3442875 remains (see photo 2). However, its functionality could not be determined to the snow cover. It could not be determined whether the culvert to where this drain empties was still clogged due to the snow and ice (see photo 3). However, it appeared to be functioning at the time of inspection, as water could be observed flowing from it (see photo 4). The ER and PPC plans were onsite (see photos 5 and 6). The ERP appeared to be adequate for this site. However, the PPC plan appeared to be unchanged since violations were issued against it. Other PCSM BMP's appeared to be installed according to plan and functioning correctly. There appeared to be 10 well bores onsite that had been SPUD (see photos 13-15). The previously noted bare spot that was mulched and seeded in response to IR 3442875 appeared to be stable at the time of inspection (see photo 17). The well site and access road appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no concerns related to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photos 12 and 18).Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued against the site PPC plan remain outstanding. Closure of violations related to the site PPC plan shall be contingent upon review by the Department upon availability after it is revised by the operator, as was stated in their NOV response.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at JKLM Energy's TSF 12 Well Site located in Lawrence Township, Tioga County on 7/30/2025 at 1110 hours. The weather was 85 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by JKLM. JKLM reported that on 7/30/2025 at ~0801 hours, a pressure regulating "Kimray" valve on a gas production unit's dump line washed out on the bottom. The washout resulted in a spray/mist of produced fluids to reach the pad surface impacting the gravel material. An estimated 25 to 35 gallons of produced fluids was released to the pad surface. An area ~16ft by 13ft by ~2 inches deep was delineated as impacted. JKLM reported that the production unit dumps ~three quarters of a barrel of produced fluids through the line at intervals and only one dump interval was able to escape the line.During my inspection, the valve was in the process of being replaced. A hydrovac truck was dispatched and was en route to the site for remediation to begin. Due to the release being under and around piping infrastructure, the hydrovac will be utilized to recover impacted material rather than using excavation equipment. The impacted area can be seen in photo #2. I field measured the pad material within the impacted area and received readings for electrical conductivity ranging from 2.7 to >4.0mS/cm. Once collected, the impacted material will be stored in a residual waste container for later disposal. A representative with JKLM will be using a soil probe to guide the remediation efforts. The hydrovac truck arrived onsite prior to my departure. JKLM later provided me with an update and photos of the area after remediation was completed (see photos #3 and 4). After removing material, it was noted that excavation efforts went 7-8 inches deep in some spots where the fluids were stopped by a soil cement layer. The area was cleaned up to visible.Based on the findings of this inspection report, the following violations are cited as immediately corrected against API #117-22232:CSL 402(b), 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a), and SWMA 301I departed the site at 1205 hours.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the STL Resources - Marshlands Play, State 822 Well Pad located in Gaines Twp, Tioga Co. on 5/25/23 at 1030 hours in response to notification of a release of 25 gallons of drilling mud (CID#372425) from a workover rig. The weather was 50 degrees, mostly sunny, winds NNE @15mph. Activity onsite consists of the Howard Drilling work-over rig and crew. Mr. Ken Shade and Mr. Seth Rodriguez were also present onsite from STL Resources. Lester Taylor, DEP OGI was also present onsite. The incident report states "At 7:15 p.m on 5/25/23, a 25 gallon spill of drilling mud occurred when a rotating annular seal on a work over rig failed due to an overpressure incident. The spill was confined to the gravel around the rig in an area estimated to be 10 feet by 10 feet. The spilled mud will be cleaned up by site personnel."As of today's inspection, the release appears to consists of diesel based drilling mud. The mud was sprayed from the failed annular seal in approximately a 12 foot radius around the rig. Mr. Rodriguez stated he believed 15-20 gallons of the mud was released to the pad surface. The spray appears to have spread further to the south side of the pad due to winds. STL used an excavator to remove the impacted pad material to the SE of the workover rig. The material was placed in a half round container located on secondary containment for disposal. Secondary containment was observed in placed under the rig vehicle and under the pipe delivery system but not under the rig itself or around the well cellar. This allowed the diesel based mud to be released to the pad surface under the rig in an approximately 12' x 20' area. Mr. Rodriguez stated they would not be able to complete removal of the impacted pad material until the rig has completed it's work-over activities and been relocated to the next well later today. Mr. Rodriguez provided an email update at 1836 hours stating the impacted pad area had been successfully remediated. STL Resources revised the estimate the diesel based drilling mud released outside of containment to ~10 gallons. The impacted area was approximately 448 sq ft with an additional 176 sq ft impacted by mist. Approximately 5 cubic yards (10 tons) of material was removed from the site. Violations of the following regulations are cited against the 1H well API#117-20741 as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED : CSL 402(b) and 25 Pa Code 78a.64(c)(1)I departed the site at 1330 hours.

Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 950243
Permit API: 117-22116
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/05/2022
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of Repsol's Johnson K 02-135 well site located in Hamilton Township, Tioga County on 4/5/2022 at 1030 hours. The weather was 54 degrees with mostly clear skies. This inspection was conducted in response to a reported release of produced water off containment. DEP Environmental Trainee, Brooke Millisock, assisted me during the inspection. ID #363183 is tied to this release within CTS. We spoke with Billy Watts (Repsol) and Ralph Babcock (Repsol) while onsite. On 4/4/2022 at approximately 1350 hours, a release of ~1 barrel of produced water to the pad surface and down the fill slope was discovered after pumping produced water from the offload tank area to the tank storage area. The release occurred due to a punctured hole in the produced water flowline. Upon discovery, flow was stopped and the pipe was wrapped with absorbents and tape to prevent additional produced water from releasing. The release was promptly reported to the DEP. Resource Environmental was dispatched to screen the impacted area and excavation was started. A third roll-off container was being utilized during today's inspection to dispose of impacted material. While onsite, the DEP screened areas within and around the excavated area. The majority of the release appears to have been cleaned up, however, a few areas were still found to be elevated in electrical conductivity. Some areas just outside of the initial excavated area were field measured at >4.00mS/cm, utilizing a Hanna GroLine soil conductivity meter. A small area near the top of the excavated area/fill slope was also field measured at >4.00mS/cm. Repsol plans to continue excavating impacted soil from the area. Based on the findings of today's inspection and based on the reported release of ~1 barrel of produced water off containment, the following violations are cited against API #117-22116 at this time: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a) 35 P.S. 6018.301 35 P.S. 691.402(b) Upon attainment with Act 2 Standards, the violations will then be closed out. We departed the site at 1145 hours.

Permit API: 081-21782
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Comments: I met Matt Casler, company man for Alta, when I arrived in response to reported spill that occurred on 10/19. Matt informed me that, during a transfer of produced water from a truck to a Baker tank, a broken valve on the truck resulted in a release of 30-40 gallons of produced water with approximately 10 gallons to the pad surface. The area had been excavated within 6-7 hours using visual confirmation that the affected material had been removed. Matt showed me the dumpster for the excavated pad material, which contained approximately 2 cubic yards of gravel and dirt. The area where the spill occurred had been re-topped with fresh gravel, and there was no indication of a spill in that area. Sitewide, there were several small (1'x1') puddles that showed slightly elevated conductance 2.08-2.86 mS/cm; Matt told me he would have them vacced. Containment and berms appeared to be in good condition, and chemical storage was clean and well maintained.

Starting at approx. 10:15, ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/15/2022
Violation Code: 78a65(a)1i - SITE RESTORATION - Post Drilling - Owner or operator failed to restore the land surface within 9 months after completion of drilling all permitted wells on the well site or 9 months after the expiration of all existing well permits on the well site, whichever is later.
Violation ID: 948144
Permit API: 047-24640
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/15/2022
Comments: This unconventional well is currently equipped for production and is equipped with a well tag displaying the well’s API number. The site ID sign at the entrance of the pad includes the required information, however it has become faded. Drilling operations were completed on this well on 12/10/2011. There is a second active well (047-24639) on this pad for which drilling operations were completed on 11/13/2011. Pin Oak has failed to restore this well site according to approved plans associated with ESX11-047-0025 and more than nine months have passed since the completion of drilling the last permitted well on this well site. Approximately one-third of this pad does not appear to be actively used for the operation of this well. There are four steel tanks labeled as holding production water located inside of a lined steel containment on this well site. At this time, the containment appears sound, as it is holding several inches of stormwater. The access road leading to this well site and well development impoundment is in general holding up to current traffic levels. There are isolated areas of scouring that should be addressed in an effort to avoid potential E&S issues in the future. Routine maintenance/improvements to the road surface should be considered prior to any heavy equipment use of the road given its proximity to Bear Creek, Little Wolf Run and several unnamed tributaries. Vegetative cover around the perimeter of the well site & well development impoundment, as well as the access road banks appears to be established. Future inspections will be conducted during the upcoming growing season to further evaluate the stabilization of earth disturbance associated with this well site & well development impoundment.

Comments: On September 18, 2024 the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Diversified's Davenport Well Site located in Derry Township, Westmoreland County in response to IR 3774486 where violations were issued for an 18-20 barrel release of production fluid from a production tank on June 4, 2024.At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared stabilized with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed and the production tank that was leaking during IR 3774486 has since been removed from the well site. A well tag was fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it, and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges was observed coming from or near the wellhead. The area where the production tank once (where the spill originated), the slope that the spill traveled down, and the area downstream where the spill pooled up at now appears to be backfilled, seeded and mulched pending vegetative growth. In addition, at the edge of the downslope area right before a forested area began, some black fencing was observed.Several soil conductivity readings were taken in the spill areas (0.0418 mS, 0.0362 mS, 0.0054 mS, 0.0137 mS, and 0.0602 mS) and are significantly lower than the soil conductivity readings taken in the same areas at the time of the spill (Soil conductivity readings taken on 6/4/24 documented in IR 3774486: 1.35 mS, 1.454 mS, Over Range, 7.63 mS, 5.51 mS, and 4.90 mS). Upon inspection of the fence, two areas appeared to be compromised. A stake appeared to be snapped and the fence appeared to be pushed down by sediment, at this time, there did not appear to be any evidence of the sediment overtopping the fence and no erosion or sedimentation was observed behind this section of fence. Another section of the fence right behind a small tree appeared to not be trenched and a gap was observed between the bottom of the fence and the ground. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed behind this section of the fence a this time either.The Department is recommending the Operator promptly properly implement and maintain the temporary erosion and sedimentation (E and S) best management practices (BMPs) to prevent any pollution from occurring.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to properly implement and maintain E and S BMPs. In addition, violations issued during IR 3774486 shall remain outstanding until the Act 2 Report is submitted, received, reviewed and approved by the Environmental Cleanup and Brownfields (ECB) Program.

Comments: This well was drilled in a forested area off of South Enterline Road in July 1997. Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-05-23
Comments: On May 23, 2019, Department representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection due to a reported incident at Rockdale Resources Harer 713 Well Pad. The Department spoke with Environmental Consultant Clayton Vioson. He said that a suction line on the AST at the Eastern end of the pad had a leak. This caused the soil under the AST to become saturated with production fluid. The area that was being excavated during the inspection was about 15' x 15'. This area was a load off area for trucks. There is another load off section that resulted in a high conductivity reading this was near the North end of the pad by the Baker tanks. The area of impact was marked and had been previously been scraped. The Department screened the North impacted area and Conductivity reading resulted 300-700 uS/cm. At the time of inspection, the impacted areas were being back filled. The release of production fluid water on the well pad is a violation of CSL 402(b), 78a56(a), and SWMA 301. The violations have been immediately corrected.

Permit API: 113-20366
Unconventional: Yes
County: Sullivan
Municipality: Forks Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/26/2024
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a release of produced fluid that occurred on 12/25/24. I spoke with Mike Demming (CHK) during the inspection. The release occurred due to produced fluid freezing in a pipe on a filter pot. The burst pipe allowed the produced fluid to spray onto the pad and into the production tank secondary containment.The impacted area of the pad was estimated to be 80' by 12'. The volume of fluid released was estimated to be between 1.5 and 2 barrels based on the fluid levels in the affected equipment. Conductivity readings were taken by CHK both on the pad surface and directly from the broken pipe. The conductivity readings were at or below 1 milliesiemen per centimeter (mS/cm). There was some black material that was released with the produced fluid.The pad surface was covered by snow and ice and did not appeared to be directly impacted. The impacted snow and frozen produced fluid were removed and placed into the production tank secondary containment. The resulting fluid in secondary containment will be removed and properly disposed of as weather permits.CHK stated that they will peruse Act 2 remediation for the release. Creston was onsite collecting Act 2 confirmation samples and screening to ensure complete removal of impacted materials. The samples will be analyzed for brine and oil contents due to the black coloring. There did not appear to be any impacts beyond those identified on the pad.The result of this inspection Violations Noted for 78a56(a) and CSL 402(b).

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/26/2026 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in North Union Township, Fayette county. OGA3216(B) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - PLAN - Failure to follow E&S control plan during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/26/2026
Violation Code: OGA3216(B) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - PLAN - Failure to follow E&S control plan during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities.
Violation ID: 8276188
Permit API: 051-23720
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: North Union Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/26/2026
Comments: On 5/26/2026, the Department conducted an at the former location of the Holchin 2 well site in North Union Township, Fayette County. This inspection follows-up to IR 4181294, where no Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) was installed at the site entrance per the Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) control plan. In response, violations were issued for failure to failure to follow the E and S plan.An NOV Response to IR 4181294 was requested from the operator by 4/30/2026. However, no response of any kind to IR 4181294 has been received from the operator at the time of this inspection. The Department issued an Order to Diversified (#445705) on August 15, 2025. According to the Order, Diversified is to restore the Well Sites within nine (9) months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 4/08/2026, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 1/08/2027 in accordance with current regulations.The following was observed during the inspection:A well plugging monument with the API number displayed was observed in the former location of the gas well (photos 19 and 20). No evidence of a spill to the surface, such as staining, was observed at the former well site location. No equipment related to well plugging and/or production was observed on site during this inspection. No evidence of nuisance mud tracking was observed from the site entrance onto Cutler Road (photo 1). The former access road and well site are temporarily stabilized and have established some vegetative growth since the time of IR 4181294, exhibiting approximately 40% vegetative growth coverage at the time of inspection. However, the third-party disturbances identified in IR 4181294 due livestock grazing continue to occur on site. The Department continues to recommend that the operator document any third-party disturbances occurring on site, and take reasonable efforts to stop them and prevent accelerated erosion from occurring on site. Temporary Erosion and sedimentation controls are installed downslope of the access road (photo 10). An access road cross-culvert is also protected by Compost Filter Sock (CFS). (photo 13) The site E and S/Restoration plans are available in a mailbox on site (photos 4-6). No evidence of accelerated erosion and sedimentation due to well plugging operations was observed on site during this inspection. However, some areas downslope of the former well site appear to lack the temporary E and S controls shown on the E and S plan drawing. Therefore, it appears that the operator continues to fail to follow the E and S control plan. Based on observations from this inspection, the violations issued in IR 4181294 shall remain outstanding. The Department recommends continued seeding and temporary stabilization on site until 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage is achieved. The violation issued in IR 4177612 for failure to post the API number on site shall be closed in IR 4205025.

Comments: On 10/24/22 at 0929 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Stonehaven Energy Mgt. Co., LLC's Wise Richard 4 well (API 065-25991) in Henderson Twp., Jefferson Co. in response to notification that the production fluid tank had overflowed. The well is located in a fenced-in area of a pasture. The well is tagged and a site ID sign is posted. The valve on the well head is open and gas could be heard escaping the pressure release valve on the separator. It was observed that production fluid has overflowed from the tank onto the ground around the separator, tank, and meter housing. The fluid was contained to the fenced-in area and did not appear to exceed 1 barrel in volume. It was observed that the tank was still filled to capacity.Violations of 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and CSL 402(b) are being cited for this inspection for the release of production fluids onto the ground. These violations will be resolved upon remediation of the site and submission of associated disposal receipts to the Department.
